clue.text: Fruit repeatedly said to cause disease

indicators.note: repeatedly means the fruit's name is given twice over
said tells us to go by how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A warning that eating some fruit again and again will make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit's name spoken twice sounds like the disease, a vitamin B1 deficiency; 'said' makes it a sound-alike and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a tropical illness caused by thiamine deficiency, so it is a named disease.

clue.text: Support little educational achievement by 15

parts.note: BAC is short for baccalaureate, the school-leaving qualification, so it is a little form of it
15 across is the chess king, abbreviated K in chess notation

explanation.surface: Backing a shortened school qualification gained alongside something else.
explanation.walkthrough: BAC shortens baccalaureate, the school-leaving exam; the puzzle has a chess mini-theme where 15 is the king, written K. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support or champion them.

clue.text: Man to cheat on bird

definitions.meaning: a chess piece is called a man, and the castle is one of them
to swindle or fleece someone out of money
a black crow-family bird that nests in colonies

explanation.surface: A man deceiving his partner with a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'on' just links the last two, and 'bird' borrows the British slang for girlfriend in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a chess piece, a verb meaning swindle, and a crow-family bird.

clue.text: Man making mistake at work

parts.note: bish is old British slang for a blunder
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone blundering on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British schoolboy slang for a mistake; the man is a chess piece in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The mitred diagonal-moving chess piece is one of the men on a chessboard.

clue.text: X-ray of man or egg — or net product

indicators.note: product means something made from the listed words, so their letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A medical scan of a person or an egg, or something made of mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' signals the anagram of MANOREGGORNET, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roentgenogram is a radiograph, named after Wilhelm Roentgen who discovered X-rays.

clue.text: Hot line to subject imprisoning 2 or 15

indicators.note: imprisoning means one piece is shut up inside another

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
R stands for rook in chess notation and also for Rex, the king

explanation.surface: A warm boundary placed under a subject that locks up chess pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Either cross-reference gives R: rook, or Rex for king.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude bounding the hot zone.

clue.text: Tit for tat is actually happening, without leave

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: something real is actually happening, not imagined
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Retaliation is taking place even though nobody has been given time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, so 'actually happening' wraps 'leave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment in kind, revenge or reward, just like tit for tat.

clue.text: Colour in picture turned into forecast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: pic is short for picture
red is a colour

indicators.note: turned means the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coloured picture that has become a weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges the word 'into' to TION, which goes after the picture holding its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction is a statement of what will happen, which is what a forecast is.

clue.text: Bless scone cooked on aircraft

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of scone are mixed up as in a recipe

parts.note: crate is slang for an old aeroplane

explanation.surface: Saying grace over a scone baked on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges SCONE to CONSE; CRATE is slang for a rickety aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make holy, to bless something for sacred use.

clue.text: Home for 2's relative on board

definitions.meaning: 2 down is a bird of the crow family, so its relative's home is the crow's dwelling
the lookout platform high on a ship's mast

explanation.surface: Where a cousin of the bird lives aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is the rook, a member of the crow family.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout perch at the masthead is named for a bird's dwelling high in a tree.

clue.text: Type of psychology relating to fugue containing right answers with piano as new heart

indicators.note: containing means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a fugue is tonal music, and its replies are called tonal answers

indicators.note: as new heart means the central letter of the word is replaced

parts.note: taken as written before its middle letter is changed
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A school of psychology concerned with a fugue that holds correct replies and a keyboard at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: In a fugue the reply to the subject can be a 'tonal answer'. 'as new heart' swaps the middle W of the answers for P, giving ANSPERS; 'containing' puts R and that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpersonal psychology is a recognised school studying spiritual experience beyond the self.

clue.text: Lady's man?

definitions.meaning: the female monarch is a lady of the highest rank
a chess piece is a man, and the most powerful one is the consort

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is a lady's man.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is': the lady is a man, a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a royal lady and also a chess piece, which players call a man.

clue.text: Worries I can't dispel on the other side

indicators.note: dispel means drive apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fears I am unable to banish on the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispel' scatters WORRIESICANT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrariwise means conversely, from the opposite standpoint.

clue.text: We take to the air in the snow (Eskimo's part, Stoppard play)

definitions.text: We take to the air in the snow

parts.note: a part of the word Eskimo's, its second to fourth letters, gives the winter sports board
Jumpers is a 1972 play by Tom Stoppard

explanation.surface: Snow-sports fliers described with an aside about an Inuit and a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Only part of the word Eskimo's is used: the run of letters after its first one. The setter's 'We' makes the definition plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski jumpers launch from a ramp and fly through the air over snow.

clue.text: Not red and not quite blue bone in antelope's back

indicators.note: in puts the other pieces inside the reversed animal
back means the animal's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: blue taken as written before trimming
the shin is the bone at the front of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Not red-faced, with a bluish bone lodged in an antelope's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the antelope round; 'not quite' trims the last letter off blue; with the bone, that sits inside the turned antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Unblushing means not going red in the face, shameless.

clue.text: Man in relation to the Godhead?

parts.note: kin are relations
the head, or first letter, of God

explanation.surface: Asking about a man's relationship with God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godhead' splits as head of God, giving G.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is the central chess piece, one of the men on the board.

clue.text: Sugar following all points to present events

indicators.note: following means the sugar comes after the compass points in the answer

parts.note: N, E, W and S are all the compass points
caster sugar is fine white sugar

explanation.surface: Sugar arriving from everywhere to mark current happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: Caster sugar is fine British baking sugar; 'following' puts it after the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscaster is the broadcaster employed to present current events, read as 'one to present events'.

clue.text: Sort of letters to sort by appearance?

parts.note: to type is to classify by kind
face means outward appearance

explanation.surface: Classifying letters by what they look like.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a design of printed characters, a kind of lettering.

clue.text: Marine received and understood on skeleton staff?

parts.note: jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine
roger is radio talk for message received

explanation.surface: A Marine acknowledging a message about a staff of reduced numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: A JOLLY is slang for a Royal Marine; the staff is a flagpole bearing skull and crossbones.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate flag shows a skull and crossbones, so it is a skeleton on a staff.

clue.text: Measure one's bottom?

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of twelve inches
the lowest part of something, as at the base of a page or mountain

explanation.surface: Taking measurements of one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a backside, but the bottom meant is the lower end of the body or of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an imperial unit of length and the lowest part of a person or thing.

clue.text: Man sees funny thing happen to 15

indicators.note: happen to says the rearranged word is attached to the cross-referenced piece

parts.note: 15 across is the chess king, written K

indicators.note: funny suggests odd, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man watches something odd befall the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges 'thing' to NIGHT, which 'happen to 15' attaches after the king's letter; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-headed chess piece is one of the men on the board.

clue.text: Give false picture of Scrooge, twisted at end here

indicators.note: twisted at end means only the final two letters swap round

parts.note: Scrooge, from Dickens, is the archetypal miser
being here means being present

explanation.surface: Distorting a portrait of Scrooge, with a twist at its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted at end' moves the E of MISER past the R, giving MISRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to describe falsely, to give a misleading account.

clue.text: Man with hand on pole

parts.note: a paw is jocular for a hand
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A man holding a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The humblest chess piece is still one of the men on the board.

clue.text: Big hit from relegated footballers?

definitions.meaning: a cut-down form of West Ham, the London club just relegated from the Premier League

explanation.surface: A smash record by a team that went down.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United were relegated in 2011; the name is shortened, as the club itself has been brought down.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham is the sound of a heavy blow, so a big hit.

clue.text: Continent deprived of morning heather

indicators.note: deprived of means letters are removed from the word

parts.note: America is a continent
am means morning, before noon

explanation.surface: A continent losing its morning heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers.

clue.text: Work on single subject to get married and hang poor result

indicators.note: result means the outcome of rearranging, so the two words become something new

explanation.surface: A treatise produced by marrying and getting a bad outcome from a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' rearranges HANGPOOR to ONOGRAPH after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A monograph is a scholarly treatise devoted to one narrow topic.

clue.text: Ring with writer backed by ten soldiers

indicators.note: backed means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A ring belonging to an author supported by a platoon of ten troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses TENGIS; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring carries a seal used in place of a signature.

clue.text: Quiet language hesitantly described as very precious?

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical sign for quiet
Latin is a language
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A soft, halting language described as treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: Platinum is a precious metal, rarer than gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metal, and a platinum award ranks above gold.
